name: 附录B 胡公庙会吹唱班部分曲目
name_en: Appendix B: Selected Repertoire of Hu Gong Temple Fair Singing Troupes
highlights: 十八狐狸又名大面姑娘，20名男演员组成，18人男扮女装
十八蝴蝶由18人饰蝴蝶，2~4人饰花神，蝴蝶翅膀用竹篾扎制
十八鲤鱼由18名女青年扮演，身背可开合红色鲤鱼壳
讨饭莲花又名永康莲花，18~36个男演员，唱《永康莲花》调
三十六行由38名男性扮演，36人扮演36个行业特征
content_zh:
十八狐狸：十八狐狸又名大面姑娘，它是方岩庙会中不可或缺的，而且是最受欢迎的节目。此舞蹈根据民间故事改编，相传唐朝有位官员原有4子18孙。后因门庭败落，17个孙子相继夭亡，撇下17个寡妇。不得已，最小的孙子迫使17位嫂嫂加上其妻共18个人开妓院、卖唱。这一舞蹈由20名男演员组成。18人男扮女装，头戴各种表情的女性面具，上穿蓝色花边大襟衣，下系黑色百褶裙，脚穿绣鞋，一手拿纸扇，一手拿绸帕。一人扮妓院老板娘，戴羊角髻大面具，穿红色花边大襟衣，系彩带，穿彩裤，着绣鞋，一手捧水烟筒，一手执麦秸扇。另一人扮嫖客，头戴瓜皮帽面具，身穿咖啡色长衫、紫黑色马褂，脚穿黑布鞋，手握长烟管。表演时，嫖客游弋于狐狸中间，丑态百出地进行挑逗调情，狐狸有的斥责反抗，有的卖弄风骚；妓院老板娘则前窜后跳，对嫖客巴结逢迎，对狐狸软哄硬压。在《望乡台》的打击乐伴奏下，只演不唱。

十八蝴蝶：十八蝴蝶由18人饰蝴蝶，2～4人饰花神。蝴蝶翅膀用竹篾扎成骨架，覆以纱布或丝绸，上绘各种花纹图案，翅膀固定在肩背上，可以自由扇动。花神为婺剧花旦打扮，上穿红色对襟水袖衫，下着百褶长裙，手曳披肩长飘带。音乐采用现成的民间小调，如《孟姜女》、《姑娘相思》等，乐队多由四人组成，两人拉二胡，一人敲钹，一人打鼓，演员只舞不唱。

十八鲤鱼：十八鲤鱼是由18名女青年扮演的大道具舞蹈。演员身背可以用双手控制自由开合的红色鲤鱼壳。鲤鱼壳的骨架用竹篾扎制，糊上彩纸或纱绸，绘上鱼身。表演时用打击乐，如大小锣、大小钹、小鼓等伴奏。

讨饭莲花：讨饭莲花又名永康莲花，一般由18～36个男演员扮演。一人扮演讨饭头，其重彩丑脸，赤膊赤脚，头戴红缨帽或草辫箍，身穿破白裙。身穿破烂衣衫的讨饭帮随后，他们每人手执一副莲花竹板，唱《永康莲花》调。通常由讨饭头领唱一句，讨饭帮跟一句腔，唱词一般有顺十字、倒十字，或即兴随编。

三十六行：三十六行是由38名男性扮演的舞蹈。其中36人扮演36个行业的特征，他们手拿各行各业的典型工具，摆出各自的架势。另有2个男演员各人头戴草辫箍，脸施重彩，衣衫不整，腰系稻草绳，赤脚，各打一面大锣，领头开路。
content_en:
Eighteen Foxes: Also known as Big-Faced Girl, this is an indispensable and most popular program at the Fangyan fair. Based on a folk tale, it tells of a Tang dynasty official with 4 sons and 18 grandsons. After the family declined, 17 grandsons died one after another, leaving 17 widows. The youngest grandson forced the 17 sisters-in-law plus his wife—18 women—to open a brothel and sing. The dance involves 20 male actors: 18 cross-dress as women, wearing various female-expression masks, blue lace-trimmed jackets, black pleated skirts, embroidered shoes, holding paper fans and silk handkerchiefs. One plays the brothel madam with a large horned-bun mask, red lace jacket, colored sash and pants, embroidered shoes, holding a water pipe and a wheat-straw fan. Another plays a client with a skullcap mask, brown long gown, purple-black mandarin jacket, black cloth shoes, and a long pipe. During performance, the client moves among the foxes, making a fool of himself with flirtation; some foxes scold and resist, others show off; the madam dashes about, fawning on the client and coercing the foxes. Accompanied by percussion music Wangxiangtai, it is acted but not sung.

Eighteen Butterflies: 18 performers play butterflies, 2-4 play flower spirits. Butterfly wings have bamboo skeletons covered with gauze or silk, painted with various patterns; the wings are fixed to the shoulders and back and can flap freely. Flower spirits are dressed as Wuju opera female leads, in red front-buttoned water-sleeve tops, long pleated skirts, and long shoulder ribbons. Music uses existing folk tunes such as Meng Jiangnu and Girl's Longing; the band usually has four people—two playing erhu, one playing cymbals, one playing drums. Performers dance but do not sing.

Eighteen Carp: A large-prop dance performed by 18 young women. Each carries a red carp shell on her back that can be opened and closed with both hands. The carp shell skeleton is made of bamboo, covered with colored paper or silk gauze, and painted with fish body patterns. Percussion instruments—large and small gongs, large and small cymbals, small drums—accompany the performance.

Begging Lotus: Also known as Yongkang Lotus, usually performed by 18-36 male actors. One plays the begging leader, with heavily made-up clown face, bare-chested and barefoot, wearing a red-tassel hat or straw-braid headband and a tattered white skirt. The begging gang in ragged clothes follows, each holding a pair of lotus bamboo clappers, singing the Yongkang Lotus tune. Usually the leader sings a line and the gang responds with a refrain; lyrics often follow shun shizi (forward ten characters) or dao shizi (reverse ten characters) patterns, or are improvised.

Thirty-Six Trades: A dance performed by 38 men. 36 portray the characteristics of 36 trades, holding typical tools of each trade and striking their poses. The other 2 wear straw-braid headbands, heavy makeup, disheveled clothes, straw ropes around their waists, barefoot, each beating a large gong and leading the way.
